title: Earlier confirmation of glaucoma progression with risk-weighted visual field and OCT scheduling
problem: Per-eye scheduling of VF and OCT repeat intervals in glaucoma
method: Longitudinal transformer risk predictor (VF, OCT RNFL, IOP, age, sex; recalibrated cumulative risk) + clinically gated decision layer choosing intervals that minimise risk-weighted detection delay plus a testing penalty fixed to a routine-testing budget; retrospective replay; Kalman and guideline comparators
data: Held-out 5,935 visits / 1,681 patients (single hospital); external VF-only adaptation on UWHVF (7,398 eyes)
claimed_novelty: Confirms simulated progression 3.4 months earlier than annual VF+OCT at comparable testing rate; allows 24-month deferral of both tests in ~20% of visits
what_they_do_NOT_do: No distribution-free / finite-sample guarantee on delayed or missed progression (authors state the budget is not a guarantee); threshold set by penalty/budget, not by conformal risk control or Learn-then-Test; goal is earlier detection at fixed budget rather than certified test avoidance; no Artes 12-week retest or GRAPE evaluation

title: Reliable and Interpretable Visual Field Progression Prediction with Diffusion Models and Conformal Risk Control
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science Medical Image Computing and Computer Assisted Intervention – MICCAI 2025
problem: Reliable VF progression forecasting with uncertainty
method: Diffusion model forecasting future VF + archetype-based conformal risk control giving finite-sample coverage on archetypal contribution intervals
data: UWHVF (28,943 VFs) and Glaucoma Research Network (602,000 VFs)
claimed_novelty: Novel archetypal conformal risk control with valid coverage and tighter intervals than pixel-wise/PUQ baselines
what_they_do_NOT_do: Uses CRC for forecast intervals, NOT for a test-deferral decision; no guarantee on delayed detection; no scheduling/test-avoidance outcome
access: full (PMC author manuscript, key sections read)

title: Using Filtered Forecasting Techniques to Determine Personalized Monitoring Schedules for Patients with Open-Angle Glaucoma
problem: Personalised VF/IOP testing schedules in open-angle glaucoma
method: Kalman filter state estimation + logistic regression for progression; algorithm schedules next VF/IOP vs fixed 1/1.5/2-year intervals
data: 571 participants from AGIS and CIGTS trials
claimed_novelty: Personalised schedules reduce diagnostic delay / improve efficiency vs fixed intervals
what_they_do_NOT_do: No ML risk model on pointwise VF; no distribution-free guarantee on delay; trial data, not real-world 24-2 archive

title: Dynamic Monitoring and Control of Irreversible Chronic Diseases with Application to Glaucoma
problem: Jointly when to monitor (next visit/tests) and how to control (target IOP) for irreversible chronic disease
method: Linear-quadratic-Gaussian state-space model; separation of estimation and control; applied to glaucoma
claimed_novelty: Optimal solution to novel LQG monitoring+control model; patient-specific monitoring and treatment plans
what_they_do_NOT_do: Model-based (parametric Gaussian) optimality, no distribution-free guarantee; no ML/deep risk model; no explicit cap on delayed detection

title: A Staged Approach to the Number and Frequency of Visual Field Testing for Detecting Glaucoma Progression
problem: Staged (intensive then down-titrated) VF review schedule vs fixed schedules
method: Computer simulation of 100,000 subjects over 30 years; staged model down-titrated after 90% of progressors in each rate bin detected; confirmation required
claimed_novelty: Staged review detects progressors with fewer tests/visits per case than fixed schedules (results truncated in abstract read)
what_they_do_NOT_do: Population-level staging rule, not per-eye risk-based deferral; simulated data only; no ML risk model; no distribution-free guarantee

title: Individualised risk assessment for diabetic retinopathy and optimisation of screening intervals: a scientific approach to reducing healthcare costs
problem: Individualised diabetic retinopathy screening intervals
method: Risk algorithm (clinical data) sets intervals so risk increase between screens equals that of annual screening
claimed_novelty: Safely extends screening intervals for most low-risk patients
what_they_do_NOT_do: Different disease; parametric risk equalisation, no distribution-free guarantee on missed progression; no VF

title: Optimizing risk-based breast cancer screening policies with reinforcement learning
problem: Personalised risk-based breast cancer screening schedules
method: Reinforcement learning (Tempo) over deep risk model outputs; trades early detection vs screening cost
data: MGH mammography; external Emory, Karolinska, Chang Gung
claimed_novelty: RL policies improve early detection at lower screening frequency
what_they_do_NOT_do: No distribution-free bound on delayed detection; different disease; reward trade-off rather than risk-controlled threshold

title: Conformal Survival Bands for Risk Screening under Right-Censoring
problem: Personalised risk screening with predictive survival bands
method: Conformal survival bands under right-censoring (IPCW + FDR multiple testing)
claimed_novelty: Flag low-risk patients with guarantee on proportion surviving past horizon (asymptotic)
what_they_do_NOT_do: Not applied to glaucoma or to scheduling repeat tests; guarantee is on flagged-set survival, not detection delay

title: Intervals between Visual Field Tests When Monitoring the Glaucomatous Patient: Wait-and-See Approach
problem: How to space VF tests over 2 years to detect rapid progression
method: Simulation of MD series with measurement variability; evenly spaced vs clustered ('wait-and-see') testing; MD linear regression; FP in stable simulated patients
claimed_novelty: Clustering tests at start and end (wait-and-see) improves power vs evenly spaced tests
what_they_do_NOT_do: Population-level fixed schedule, not individual risk-based deferral; no ML; no guarantee on delay

title: Frequency of Testing to Detect Visual Field Progression Derived Using a Longitudinal Cohort of Glaucoma Patients
problem: Time to detect VF progression for different testing frequencies
method: Variability estimated from cohort; simulation of real-world VF series; MD trend with 2 baselines + confirmation
data: 1,072 eyes / 665 patients (UCSD) used to parameterise simulations
claimed_novelty: e.g., 80% of -2 dB/yr eyes detected at 3.3/2.4/2.1 yrs with 1/2/3 tests per year; recommends semiannual testing early
what_they_do_NOT_do: Fixed frequencies only; no per-eye adaptive deferral; no ML; no statistical guarantee

title: Practical recommendations for measuring rates of visual field change in glaucoma
problem: Number/frequency of VF exams needed to measure rates of MD change
method: Statistical power modelling from empirical MD variability
claimed_novelty: Recommends ~3 VFs/yr in first 2 years to detect rapid progression
what_they_do_NOT_do: Fixed population recommendation; no individual adaptive schedule or ML

title: Progression detection in glaucoma can be made more efficient by using a variable interval between successive visual field tests
venue: Graefe's Archive for Clinical and Experimental Ophthalmology
problem: Optimal spacing of VF tests for progression detection
method: Simulation in theoretical cohort; fixed 3/6-month vs variable interval (yearly until suspicion, then prompt confirmation)
claimed_novelty: Variable interval makes progression detection more efficient
what_they_do_NOT_do: Rule-based adaptivity, no learned risk model, no guarantee on delay

title: Time to Identify Glaucoma Progression Given Typical Visual Field Testing Frequencies in a US Nationwide Insured Population
problem: Time to identify trend-based VF progression at real-world US testing frequencies vs annual testing
method: Simulation using clinical VF data; testing intervals at 25th/50th/75th percentile of US claims (median 1.59 yr) vs annual
data: Duke Glaucoma Registry VF data; US claims frequencies
claimed_novelty: Quantifies detection delay from under-testing in US practice
what_they_do_NOT_do: Opposite direction (harm of infrequent testing); no individual deferral rule; no ML; no guarantee

title: Reinforcement learning for individualized lung cancer screening schedules: A nested case–control study
problem: Individualised lung cancer screening schedules
method: Reinforcement learning on nodule features in nested case-control NLST data
claimed_novelty: RL policies personalise follow-up intervals
what_they_do_NOT_do: No distribution-free guarantee; different disease

title: Conformal selective prediction with cost aware deferral for safe clinical triage under distribution shift
problem: Safe clinical triage with deferral to clinicians
method: Split / Mondrian / importance-weighted conformal prediction + cost-aware deferral threshold on calibration set
data: Early sepsis prediction data, temporally separated ID/OOD splits
claimed_novelty: Selective deferral reduces error on retained cases ~50% at 80% coverage
what_they_do_NOT_do: Deferral = hand to human, not skipping a future test; threshold chosen by expected cost (not risk-controlled); no longitudinal monitoring

title: RetinaGuard: Risk-Controlled Agentic Triage for Multi-Disease Retinal Screening
problem: Which automated retinal-screening decisions can be accepted without review
method: Agentic triage with learned failure predictor; acceptance threshold certified by conformal risk control
claimed_novelty: At nominal 5% unsafe level accepts 37% of cases vs 10% for confidence referral
what_they_do_NOT_do: Cross-sectional image triage, not longitudinal test deferral; not glaucoma VF

title: Conformal Risk Control
problem: Controlling expected value of any monotone loss with conformal calibration
method: Conformal risk control (finite-sample bound on expected loss via threshold calibration)
claimed_novelty: Generalises split conformal to arbitrary bounded monotone losses
what_they_do_NOT_do: Methodology only; no clinical monitoring/deferral application

title: Learn then test: Calibrating predictive algorithms to achieve risk control
problem: Calibrating predictive algorithms to control risk with high probability
method: Learn-then-Test: multiple hypothesis testing over thresholds with valid p-values
claimed_novelty: High-probability risk control for arbitrary (non-monotone) risks
what_they_do_NOT_do: Methodology only; no VF / follow-up scheduling application

title: Beyond Point Estimates for Glaucoma Visual Field Forecasting with Diffusion Models
problem: Probabilistic VF forecasting
method: Conditioned denoising diffusion models generating distributions of future VFs with irregular intervals
claimed_novelty: Well-calibrated distributions; SOTA point accuracy
what_they_do_NOT_do: No decision rule for deferral; calibration is model-based, no distribution-free guarantee on delay

title: Forecasting Risk of Future Rapid Glaucoma Worsening Using Early Visual Field, OCT, and Clinical Data
problem: Forecast future rapid VF worsening from early VF/OCT/clinical data
method: Vision transformer feature extractor on VF/OCT stack + clinical data; linear classifier
claimed_novelty: AUC 0.87 for rapid worsening with 3 VFs + OCT + clinical
what_they_do_NOT_do: Risk prediction only; no scheduling/deferral rule; no risk-controlled threshold

title: Predicting eyes at risk for rapid glaucoma progression based on an initial visual field test using machine learning
problem: Predict rapid progression (MD < -1 dB/yr) from initial VF
method: SVM, ANN etc. on summary/pointwise VF + age
claimed_novelty: Initial VF predicts rapid progression with AUC ~0.72
what_they_do_NOT_do: Baseline risk only; no visit-level deferral; no guarantee

title: Deep learning of longitudinal visual fields predicts glaucoma progression rate and identifies fast progressors
problem: Predict MD/VFI progression rates and fast progressors from longitudinal VF
method: GLAM: attention-based fusion of 24-2 TD sequences + clinical features, aleatoric uncertainty
claimed_novelty: MD-rate MAE 0.139 dB/yr, AUC 0.99 for fast progressors
what_they_do_NOT_do: No scheduling/deferral; no distribution-free calibration

title: Longitudinal Risk Prediction for Pediatric Glioma with Temporal Deep Learning
problem: 1-year recurrence prediction for pediatric glioma from serial MRI
method: Self-supervised temporal learning: classify correct chronological order of a patient's scans as pretext, then fine-tune
claimed_novelty: Temporal-order pretraining improves recurrence prediction F1 up to 58.5%
what_they_do_NOT_do: Not VF; order task used for pretraining only, not as a calibrated test statistic; no scheduling

title: Visual Field Progression in Glaucoma: Estimating the Overall Significance of Deterioration with Permutation Analyses of Pointwise Linear Regression (PoPLR)
problem: Overall significance of VF deterioration in an individual eye
method: Truncated product of pointwise regression p-values (S); p-value from within-series permutation of test order
claimed_novelty: Exact per-eye permutation p-value; better than PLR criteria
what_they_do_NOT_do: Hand-crafted statistic; not a learned model; no scheduling

title: Visual Field Progression in Glaucoma: Comparison Between PoPLR and ANSWERS
problem: Compare PoPLR vs ANSWERS
method: Positive rate on real series; false-positive rate by permuting the same series
claimed_novelty: Modelling variability/spatial correlation does not clearly beat simple PoPLR (per abstract framing)
what_they_do_NOT_do: No learned statistic; no scheduling

title: Self-supervised denoising of visual field data improves detection of glaucoma progression
problem: Denoise VF to improve progression detection
method: Self-supervised masked autoencoder and VAE (with pointwise p-values) for denoising; PLR on denoised data
claimed_novelty: 4.7% more progressing eyes detected by PLR; 2.3 months earlier
what_they_do_NOT_do: Self-supervision is reconstruction (masking), not temporal order; no permutation calibration of a learned statistic; no scheduling

title: More Accurate Modeling of Visual Field Progression in Glaucoma: ANSWERS
problem: More accurate VF progression modelling
method: ANSWERS: non-stationary Weibull error regression + spatial enhancement; compared with MD LR and PoPLR
data: UKGTS VF series (9,104 SITA tests, up to 2 years)
claimed_novelty: Higher detection at matched specificity by modelling variability/spatial correlation
what_they_do_NOT_do: Parametric model; no learned statistic; no scheduling

title: Visual Field Progression in Glaucoma
problem: Per-patient specificity of GPA
method: GPA applied to 12 tests in 3 months with 1000 random reorderings
claimed_novelty: Mean FP 2.6% (likely) / 18.5% (possible) after 10 tests; strong between-patient variation
what_they_do_NOT_do: No ML; no scheduling; but provides the short-term retest dataset planned for use

title: Hierarchical Censored Bayesian Analysis of Visual Field Progression
problem: Bayesian VF progression model handling censoring and heteroskedasticity
method: Hierarchical censored heteroskedastic Bayesian model; FPR matched via permutations of test-retest cohort
claimed_novelty: Better hit-rate/time-to-progression at matched FPR
what_they_do_NOT_do: No scheduling/deferral; no distribution-free threshold

title: Development and Comparison of Machine Learning Algorithms to Determine Visual Field Progression
problem: ML classifiers to determine VF progression
method: LR, RF, XGB, SVC, CNN, FCNN on half-series averages; labels from 6 conventional algorithms incl. PoPLR
claimed_novelty: MLCs 87-91% accurate, comparable to conventional algorithms
what_they_do_NOT_do: Supervised on algorithm labels; no permutation calibration; no scheduling

title: Assessing Glaucoma Progression Using Machine Learning Trained on Longitudinal Visual Field and Clinical Data
problem: Detect progression from longitudinal VF + clinical data
method: Convolutional LSTM on 4 consecutive VFs ± clinical data; labels from VFI/MD slope and PLR
claimed_novelty: 91-93% accuracy; clinical data improves AUC
what_they_do_NOT_do: Supervised labels; no false-positive control by permutation; no scheduling

title: An Artificial Intelligence Approach to Detect Visual Field Progression in Glaucoma Based on Spatial Pattern Analysis
problem: Detect VF progression via spatial pattern change
method: Archetypal analysis (16 archetypes) + regression of archetype weights
claimed_novelty: Archetype method detects progression earlier/more than MD, AGIS, CIGTS etc.
what_they_do_NOT_do: No scheduling; normal limits from population, not within-eye permutation

title: Efficacy of Smoothing Algorithms to Enhance Detection of Visual Field Progression in Glaucoma
problem: Smoothing VFs to enhance progression detection
method: Nearest-neighbour and VAE smoothing before mTD/VFI rates, PLR, PoPLR, GRI; noiseless simulation for specificity
claimed_novelty: Smoothing increases proportion of progressing eyes detected
what_they_do_NOT_do: No learned order statistic; no scheduling

title: Comparison of Visual Field Point-Wise Event-Based and Global Trend-Based Analysis for Detecting Glaucomatous Progression
problem: Compare GPA event vs MD/VFI trend analysis
method: Simulation from real cohort with specificity matched on simulated stable eyes
claimed_novelty: Trend vs event sensitivity compared at matched specificity
what_they_do_NOT_do: No ML; no scheduling

title: Forecasting future Humphrey Visual Fields using deep learning
problem: Forecast future 24-2 HVFs
method: Deep CNN pointwise forecasting with transfer learning across time intervals
data: University of Washington HVFs 1998-2018 (source of UWHVF)
claimed_novelty: DL can forecast HVF up to 5.5 years
what_they_do_NOT_do: Forecasting only; no deferral rule or guarantee

title: Estimating Rates of Progression and Predicting Future Visual Fields in Glaucoma Using a Deep Variational Autoencoder
problem: Rates of progression and prediction of future VFs
method: Generalised variational autoencoder latent space rates
claimed_novelty: VAE latent rates detect progression earlier than MD rates
what_they_do_NOT_do: No scheduling; no guarantee

title: Predicting Longitudinal Visual Field Progression With Class Imbalanced Data
venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
problem: Predict VF progression from longitudinal VF with class imbalance
method: VF-Transformer with inverted class-dependent temperature loss
data: Public VF dataset + external hospital dataset
claimed_novelty: Handles class imbalance for longitudinal VF progression prediction
what_they_do_NOT_do: No scheduling or guarantee

title: The Frontloading Fields Study (FFS): Detecting Changes in Mean Deviation in Glaucoma Using Multiple Visual Field Tests Per Clinical Visit
problem: Number of VF tests per visit and follow-up interval for detecting MD change
method: Simulation of 10,000 progressing and 10,000 stable patients from intra/intersession data
data: 322 intrasession / 323 intersession patients used to model
claimed_novelty: Two tests per visit greatly increase detection and shorten time to detection; FP <2.5%
what_they_do_NOT_do: Fixed protocols; no individual risk-based deferral; no ML

title: Surveillance of sight loss due to delay in ophthalmic treatment or review: frequency, cause and outcome
problem: Frequency/causes of sight loss due to NHS-initiated delay in review or treatment
method: Prospective national active surveillance (BOSU) questionnaire
claimed_novelty: Glaucoma 42% of harm cases; delayed follow-up is main cause; capacity shortfall
what_they_do_NOT_do: Motivation only (harm of delay); no deferral method

title: A Hybrid Deep Learning–Based Approach for Visual Field Test Forecasting
problem: Pointwise VF forecasting with fewer prior tests
method: Hybrid RNN + CNN with depthwise transformers (Hybrid-VF-Net)
claimed_novelty: Improved forecasting accuracy/flexibility
what_they_do_NOT_do: No deferral decision; no guarantee

title: Artificial Intelligence-Guided Endpoint Selection for Neuroprotection Trials in Glaucoma
problem: Predict locations most likely to progress for trial endpoint selection
method: Graph attention network on baseline TD values
data: 82,449 SAP tests / 14,237 eyes: Bascom Palmer, Duke, UWHVF
claimed_novelty: Targeted High-5 endpoint enriches progression detection
what_they_do_NOT_do: Trial enrichment, not clinical test deferral

title: DeepAtrophy: Teaching a neural network to detect progressive changes in longitudinal MRI of the hippocampal region in Alzheimer's disease
problem: Detect progressive hippocampal change from longitudinal MRI
method: CNN trained self-supervised to order scan pairs and infer interval ratios; output used as atrophy score
claimed_novelty: Temporal-inference network yields progression measure robust to registration artifacts
what_they_do_NOT_do: Not VF; no per-subject permutation p-value; no scheduling

title: Learning-based inference of longitudinal image changes: Applications in embryo development, wound healing, and aging brain
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
problem: Quantify individual longitudinal image change
method: LILAC: Siamese CNN trained to predict temporal order / difference of image pairs
claimed_novelty: Temporal ordering accuracy >0.98; learned differences track real change
what_they_do_NOT_do: Not VF; no hypothesis-test calibration; no scheduling

title: Learning to Compare Longitudinal Images
problem: Compare longitudinal images ignoring nuisance variation
method: PaIRNet pairwise ranking network; self-supervised temporal ordering
claimed_novelty: Localises/quantifies meaningful change while discounting nuisance
what_they_do_NOT_do: Not VF; no per-subject permutation test

title: Modeling Disease Progression In Retinal OCTs With Longitudinal Self-Supervised Learning
problem: Model AMD progression from longitudinal OCT
method: Self-supervised prediction of time interval between same-patient scan pairs; transfer to AMD conversion
claimed_novelty: Time-interval pretext yields progression-specific representation
what_they_do_NOT_do: Not VF; no test calibration

title: The classification permutation test: A flexible approach to testing for covariate imbalance in observational studies
problem: Covariate balance testing
method: Classification Permutation Test: classifier accuracy as statistic, permutation null
claimed_novelty: Flexible nonparametric balance test with exact permutation validity
what_they_do_NOT_do: Not longitudinal/medical monitoring; no scheduling

title: Learning and Using the Arrow of Time
venue: 2018 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
problem: Self-supervised arrow-of-time classification in video
method: Deep network trained to predict forward vs reversed playback
claimed_novelty: Arrow of time as self-supervised signal and representation
what_they_do_NOT_do: Not medical

title: Shuffle and Learn: Unsupervised Learning Using Temporal Order Verification
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science Computer Vision – ECCV 2016
problem: Unsupervised representation learning from video
method: Temporal order verification of shuffled frame tuples
claimed_novelty: Order verification as pretext task
what_they_do_NOT_do: Not medical

title: Unsupervised Gaussian Mixture-Model With Expectation Maximization for Detecting Glaucomatous Progression in Standard Automated Perimetry Visual Fields
problem: Detect progression along VF defect patterns
method: Unsupervised GEM / VIM mixture models; confidence limit from 84 stable eyes
claimed_novelty: GEM-POP sensitive for progression at set specificity
what_they_do_NOT_do: No scheduling; no within-eye permutation

title: CHIASM: A Self-Supervised Visual Field Encoder for Neuro-Ophthalmology
problem: Self-supervised VF encoder to flag neurological (vertical-meridian) VF loss
method: Masked autoencoder on pattern deviation; linear classifier on latent dims
data: Pretrain 23,223 UWHVF VFs; external Harvard-GF 3,300 patients
claimed_novelty: Anatomically interpretable latent dims; balanced acc 0.78 for neurological patterns
what_they_do_NOT_do: Cross-sectional; no temporal-order pretext; no progression testing; no scheduling

title: Revisiting Classifier Two-Sample Tests
problem: Two-sample testing with classifiers
method: Classifier two-sample test (held-out accuracy, permutation/binomial null)
claimed_novelty: C2ST competitive and interpretable
what_they_do_NOT_do: Not medical monitoring

title: Labeling matters: A multicenter machine learning study on visual field progression in Glaucoma
problem: Effect of label definition on ML VF progression detection
method: SVM/RF/LR/XGB trained on Consensus vs Wiggs' labels
data: Multicentre VF data, 5 Korean tertiary hospitals
claimed_novelty: Performance strongly depends on labelling strategy
what_they_do_NOT_do: No scheduling; supervised

title: UWHVF: A Real-World, Open Source Dataset of Perimetry Tests From the Humphrey Field Analyzer at the University of Washington
problem: Open real-world HFA 24-2 dataset
method: Data descriptor; LR progression on global/regional/pointwise values
claimed_novelty: First large open-source HVF dataset
what_they_do_NOT_do: Not a method paper

title: GRAPE: A multi-modal dataset of longitudinal follow-up visual field and fundus images for glaucoma management
problem: Open longitudinal VF + fundus dataset for glaucoma management
method: Data descriptor
claimed_novelty: Multimodal longitudinal glaucoma dataset
what_they_do_NOT_do: Not a method paper

title: Optimizing Structure–Function Relationship by Maximizing Correspondence Between Glaucomatous Visual Fields and Mathematical Retinal Nerve Fiber Models
problem: Optimise RNFL structure-function model from VF correlations (Rotterdam data)
method: Correlation of age-adjusted VF location pairs vs RNFL model distances
data: 103 VFs of moderately damaged eyes (Rotterdam Eye Hospital)
claimed_novelty: Optimised RNFL model; noise reduction in VFs
what_they_do_NOT_do: Not a monitoring/scheduling paper (cited as Rotterdam dataset source)
